15. The Great Decisive Analysis of the Solitary Ground, the Non-Distraction, the Certainty, and the Certain Path. Thus has been explained the Great Decisive Analysis of the Sovereign King of Heights, which consists of the quantity of all space and all atoms. Next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Solitary Ground, the Non-Distraction, the Certainty, and the Certain Path shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Even amidst roads that are not confused, There is also the stage of the vajra.
In each and every position, because there exists a fundamental unity, the number one hundred and two is established.
Thus, there are five kinds of repetitions: namely, the "one above," the "one fundamental," and the "one."
"Simultaneous revolution and non-confusion constitute the stage of perfect fulfillment.
The commentary states:

Within the divisions of the paths of individual stages that are unmixed and fixed, there are likewise fifty-one kinds of True Vajra stages; in each and every stage, there exists its own fundamental essence.

For this reason, the number one hundred and two is established; as the verse states: "Even within the non-chaotic path, there is also the Vajra stage; because each and every stage retains its original 'one,' the number one hundred and two is formed."
Based on these stages, there are five types of established modes of transformation (*parivṛtti-lakṣaṇa*).

What are the five? First, the gate of successive and individual transformation; second, the gate of fundamental and fundamental individual transformation; third, the gate of simultaneous and inseparable transformation; fourth, the gate of distinct and unmixed transformation; fifth, the gate of complete and perfect transformation. These are the five, as stated in the verse: "Based on the stages, the modes of transformation are established; thus there are five kinds of layers: namely, the superior, the fundamental, the individual, the simultaneous, the unmixed, and the stage of complete perfection."
What is the characteristic of the first turning?
The verse says:
"In fifty-one types of states, each one individually encompasses fifty."
They turn at one time and in one place, yet they cannot be unified.
The commentary asks:
What is meant by "each individual gate" (一一門) of the above?
Regarding what are called the fifty-one stages, each and every stage encompasses the turning of fifty-one times and locations.
If this were so, they would have to be combined into a single entity.

Each functions individually and cannot be unified, as the verse states: "The fifty-one stages each encompass fifty; they function simultaneously and in a single location, yet they cannot be unified. Thus it is said.
Having thus explained the gate of the successive transformations of each of the higher stages, next we shall explain the gate of the successive transformations of each of the fundamental stages.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
Fifty-one texts as one, each one encompassing fifty;
they turn simultaneously in a single place, yet they cannot be merged into one.
The Treatise says:
What is meant by the "fundamental individual gates"?
This refers to the fifty-one fundamental types, wherein each and every one of these fifty-one types individually encompasses the manifestation of fifty-one times and locations.
If that were so, their collection would have to constitute a single entity.

However, because each functions individually, they cannot be unified, as the verse states: "The fifty-one are fundamentally one, yet each one encompasses the fifty; though they function simultaneously in a single location, they cannot be unified."
Having thus explained the gate of the mutual transformation of each fundamental and derivative [consciousness], next we shall explain the gate of their simultaneous and inseparable transformation.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
The fundamental one and the subsequent one, Mutually encompass all stages;
They function together without separation, Yet they cannot be merged into one.
The Commentary says:
What is called the "gate of simultaneous operation"?

It refers to the fact that the fifty-one factors of the fundamental [set] each individually encompass the fifty-one factors of the subsequent [set], and those fifty-one factors of the subsequent set are likewise able to encompass the former; because they operate simultaneously and revolve together without separation, yet each functions at its own distinct time and place and cannot be merged into one. As the verse says: "The fundamental and the subsequent / Mutually encompass all stages / Operating together without abandonment / Yet they cannot be merged into one."

Thus has been explained the gateway of the mode of operation that proceeds concomitantly and without separation; next, the gateway of the mode of operation that proceeds distinctly and without intermixture shall be explained.
What is its characteristic?
The verse says:
In all stages from the fundamental to the ultimate,
each and every one dwells securely within its own domain, because it does not encompass the dharmas of others.
The Commentary says:
What is called the "gate of distinct non-intermixture"?

It refers to all the various fundamental and derivative stages (*pada*), each of which dwells solely within its own domain, neither shifting nor entering or exiting, neither encompassing others nor being fixed as permanent; for they are eternally complete, pervasive, and vast. As the verse says: "All fundamental and derivative stages, each and every one, dwell within their own domain, because they do not encompass other dharmas."
Thus has been explained the gate of the distinct and unmixed modes of transformation; next, the gate of the complete and perfect modes of transformation shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
The four gates previously explained, which function with unimpeded mastery at all times and in all places, are called "fully perfected.
The treatise says:
What is meant by "the gate of complete transformation"? It refers to the four gates previously described:

simultaneous transformation and transformation in a single location; transformation at different times and in different locations; singular transformation and distinct transformation; and collective transformation and individual transformation. Because these occur with unimpeded mastery, as the verse says: "The four gates previously described, in all times and places, transform with unimpeded mastery; this is called complete perfection."
In the *Mahāyāna-mahādhāraṇī-vajra-mantra-sūtra*, it is stated as follows:

"Within the ocean of the Dharma-treasury gates—each and every one of which is entirely free from the confusion of existence and non-existence, and each of which possesses a single name and a single measure—there are, in total, two dharmas."
What are the two? First is the general, and second is the specific.
As for the specific, it refers to the four types of universal wheels (cakra).
Regarding the term "comprehensive," it is because the four types of wheels all revolve with sovereign mastery.
This is as explained at length [in the source]. Section Sixteen:

The Great Determinative Analysis of the Single, Vast, Non-dual Mountain King of the Solitary Ground and the Solitary Heaven. Thus has been explained the Great Determinative Analysis of the Path of Certainty and Non-confusion regarding the Solitary Ground. Next, the Great Determinative Analysis of the Single, Vast, Non-dual Mountain King of the Solitary Ground and the Solitary Heaven shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the substance of this king of mountains, there are two kinds of gates.
That is to say, regarding the fundamental nature and the primordial source, they should be observed in their respective order.
The treatise states:
Within this single, vast, non-dual body of the mountain king—consisting of a solitary stage and a solitary heaven—there are two gates.
What are the two? First, the gate of the stage of the original single intrinsic nature; second, the gate of the fundamental stage of the original one. These are called the two.

One should examine these in their proper sequence, as the verse states: "Within the substance of this king of mountains, there are two kinds of gates; namely, the self-nature and the primordial source; they should be examined in that order."
What are the characteristics of the stage of the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*)?
The verse says:
Within that single fundamental dharma, it is spontaneous and independent of others.
There are fifty-one stages; these are called the stages of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*).
Thus, within each of these fifty-one, there are five hundred dharma-gates, revolving everywhere and extensively.
The Treatise says:
What is meant by the "stages of intrinsic nature" (*svabhāva-bhūmi*)?

It refers to the fact that within the fifty-one kinds of original, single dharmas previously mentioned, each and every one possesses fifty-one true vajra stages through its own natural intrinsic nature, independent of any external force. Therefore, they are called the "stages of intrinsic nature," as the verse states: "Within that original single dharma, naturally and without depending on others, there are fifty-one stages; these are named the stages of intrinsic nature."

Thus, each of these fifty-one stages contains a great ocean of five hundred dharma-gates; these turn everywhere and turn extensively, as the verse states: "In this way, each and every one of the fifty-one [stages] possesses five hundred dharma-gates, which turn everywhere and turn extensively."
Within this stage, one should carefully examine and discern the five great gates as previously described, ensuring they are fully complete and perfectly fulfilled.
Thus has been explained the gate of the stage of the fundamental single self-nature; next, the gate of the fundamental stage of the fundamental one shall be explained.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
The fifty-one primary dharmas each also have their own primary dharmas.
"Named 'Emptiness of Emptiness,' it is one; within this, there are also stages.
The Commentary says:

Within the "Emptiness of Emptiness" that serves as the basis for the original "One," there are likewise various stages. Each and every stage consists of one hundred thousand dharma-gates, which turn in complete perfection and without deficiency.
Within this stage, there are also the five great gates previously mentioned; one should carefully examine and discern them as being fully complete and perfectly fulfilled.
The *Sūtra on the Treatise on the Chapters* states:
"Within the essence of the Mahāyāna of meditative concentration, there are three great gates."
What are these three?

First, the gate of the vast ocean-like assembly established in the higher stages; second, the gate of the single existence of the fundamental source; third, the gate of the single emptiness of the fundamental emptiness of emptiness.
"Thus, all three gates possess various stages, which are fully perfected and characterized by both identical and differing modes of revolution," and so forth,
as explained at length. *The Great Treatise on the Mysterious Source Text of the Grand Foundation*, Scroll Eight.
The Treatise on the Profound Fundamental Text of the Great Totality, Volume Nine.
Composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;
translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha.

17. The Great Section on the Decisive Determination of the Sovereign Path of the Peerless Mountain King. Thus has been explained the Great Section on the Decisive Determination of the Peerless Mountain King, which is the singular ground, the singular heaven, the one vast and non-dual sovereign. Next, the Great Section on the Decisive Determination of the Sovereign Path of the Peerless Mountain King shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of mastery, there are a total of a thousand successive turns.
This means that within each of the "original," "superior," and "middle" [sections], there are five hundred [subdivisions] respectively.
The Treatise says:

Within this section on the sovereign paths of the two mountain kings, there are a total of one thousand distinct layers of mutual transformation; that is to say, because there are five hundred each in the original, superior, and middle [sections]. As the verse states: "Within the sovereign paths, there are a total of one thousand transformations, because there are five hundred each in the original, superior, and middle."
How does the transformation of the fundamental [nature] correspond?
The verse says:
The fundamental turns once toward [the derivative]; One is empty and one is existent as it turns.
Up to the five hundredth, and the remaining positions are likewise.
The treatise asks:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?

In order to manifest the downward progression from the single fundamental gate, there is one Vajra-emptiness and one Vajra; appearing one by one in succession according to their order, they gradually enter into the sequence up to the five hundredth.

In this manner, throughout the other successive stages as well, one gradually enters until reaching the five hundredth stage; it is inexhaustible, boundless, and without beginning or end, because it revolves perpetually, perfectly, and extensively. As the verse says: "From the original one, there is a downward revolution; with one emptiness and one existence, one revolves until the five hundredth stage; the other stages are likewise."
The successive transformations of the higher stages should be understood by analogy with this.
The *Sūtra on the Nature and Virtues of the Cause of Illumination* states:
"The Dharma-treasury of the Father and Son, the non-dual One Vehicle, proceeds through successive higher transformations; it has a beginning and an end, yet it is without exhaustion."
Descending and descending further, there is a beginning and an end, yet it is without exhaustion.
That which has a beginning and an end refers to the progression from the stages of faith and so forth up to the measure of five hundred.
"It is inexhaustible because the ocean of the Dharma-treasury is extremely vast," and so forth, as explained at length. The Eighteenth Section:

The Great Determinative Analysis of the Single Ground of the Supreme High Peak of the Mahādvaya Mountain King. Thus has been explained the Great Determinative Analysis of the Sovereign Path of the Solitary and Peerless Mountain King. Next, the Great Determinative Analysis of the Single Ground of the Supreme High Peak of the Mahādvaya Mountain King shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Fundamentally and supremely inexhaustible, It is established with such a name.
All remaining stages should also be understood in this same way.
The treatise says:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?

This is because it is intended to manifest that the fundamental-fundamental is infinitely inexhaustible, the superior-superior is infinitely inexhaustible; the fundamental-superior is infinitely inexhaustible, the superior-fundamental is infinitely inexhaustible; each and every one is infinitely inexhaustible, the many are infinitely inexhaustible; the same is infinitely inexhaustible, the different is infinitely inexhaustible; the equal is infinitely inexhaustible, the distinct is infinitely inexhaustible; the finite is infinitely inexhaustible, the infinite is infinitely inexhaustible—pervasive, vast, complete, and perfect. As the verse says: "The fundamental-superior is infinitely inexhaustible, and thus this name is established; all remaining stages should likewise be understood in this way."
The *Mahāyānasamudrasūtra* states as follows:
"Within the ocean of the Mahāyāna of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), one thousand two hundred inexhaustible categories (*akṣayapada*) are fully present and turn together."
...and so forth, as explained at length.
*The Great Treatise on the Mysterious Source Text of the Great Mass of the Ground*, Scroll Nine;
*The Great Treatise on the Mysterious Source Text of the Great Mass of the Ground*, Scroll Ten.
Composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;
translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha.

Chapter Nineteen: The Great Determination of the Path of the *Gandhavatī-vijaya-krama*. Thus, the Great Determination of the Single Ground at the Most Victorious High Summit of the Mahādvaya-parvatarāja has already been explained. Next, the Great Determination of the Path of the *Gandhavatī-vijaya-krama* shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of the *khaṇḍa* and *vīthi*, there are seven transformations corresponding to cultivation.
It is taken as the measure of the path, and no other characteristic exists.
The commentary says:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?

This is because it is intended to demonstrate that within the path of the *śīla* (stages of purification), the measure of its boundaries consists solely of the sevenfold transformation (*sapta-parivarta*), as there are no other characteristics. As the verse states: "Within the path of the *śīla*, one practices through the sevenfold transformation; this constitutes the measure of the path, for there are no other modes of conduct."
What is called the sevenfold transformative cultivation?
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
The seven transformations are of three kinds: merit, faults, and so forth;
within the fifty-one stages, these seven transformations revolve upward and downward, increasing the categories of merit as well as the ocean of afflictions.
The treatise says:
Regarding the sevenfold transformative practices, how many types are there in total?
There are three kinds.

What are the three? First, the sevenfold transformation of merit; second, the sevenfold transformation of faults; and third, the sevenfold transformation of equality. These are called the three, as the verse states: "The sevenfold transformations are of three kinds: merit, faults, and equality."

Regarding what is called "transformative aspects" (*pariṇāma-lakṣaṇa*): within the fifty-one stages of the Vajra-position, there are seven transformations consisting of upward shifts and downward shifts. This is because they involve the vast transformation of increasing merit and increasing afflictions. As the verse states: "Within the fifty-one stages, there are seven upward and downward transformations, which increase the categories of merit as well as the ocean of various afflictions."
Furthermore, what are the characteristics of the seven transformations of the calamities?
The verse says:
In the very first transformation, each [of the three realms] increases by a hundredfold.
Each subsequent stage increases by a thousand, each obstructing one or two virtues;
in the final six stages, the increase changes accordingly, doubling at each successive turn.
The Treatise says:
In the first transformation, by how many numbers does it increase as it revolves?
How many pure dharmas does it obstruct?
This means that during the process of upward progression, within each respective stage (*bhūmi*), one hundred categories of afflictions (*kleśa*) increase, obstructing one pure dharma.

If, during the process of descending, each successive stage increases by a thousand categories of afflictions that obstruct the two pure dharmas—as stated in the verse: "In the first transformation, the upper [stages] each increase by a hundred, while the lower [stages] each increase by a thousand; each obstructs one or two virtues. Thus it is said.

Regarding the virtues and faults within the latter six transformations, because they increase by doubling in successive order, as the verse states: "In the latter six transformations, respectively, they turn by doubling the number of times."
Thus, having already explained the sevenfold gate of manifesting faults, next the sevenfold gate of manifesting virtues shall be explained.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
In the first transformation, the upper realms each increase by one hundred million, while the lower realms each increase by two hundred million; these changes proceed gradually in successive order.
In the subsequent six transformations, they increase according to the sequence by doubling the number at each step.
Without destroying the number of afflictions, they manifest as meritorious transformations.
The commentary says:
In the first transformation, by how many numbers does it increase and evolve?
This means that during the upward progression, in each successive stage, one increases by one hundred million categories of merit, progressing gradually.
During the downward progression, in each successive stage, one increases by two hundred million categories of merit, progressing gradually.

As the verse states: "In the first transformation, each upper [region] increases by one hundred million, and each lower [region] increases by two hundred million, gradually turning in successive order.

Because in the subsequent six transformations, the numbers increase by doubling in their respective order, as the verse says: "In the latter six transformations, they turn by successively doubling the number."
Regarding these categories of merit and afflictions, are they abandoned or not?
They merely undergo transformation and evolution, for they are neither moved nor destroyed. As the verse says: "Without destroying the number of faults, one transforms them into merit."
Having thus explained the gate of the sevenfold transformations that manifest merit, next I shall explain the gate of the sevenfold transformations that manifest equality.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
In the first transformation, each [period] increases by one thousand at the top and decreases by twenty thousand at the bottom; the quantities thus shift gradually.
In the subsequent six transformations, they increase respectively by doubling the number at each step.
There is no distinction in the severance of obstructions; it is established solely by way of measure.
The treatise says:
In the first transformation, how many numbers increase as they revolve?
This means that during the upward progression, one thousand [moments] are added at each successive stage as they proceed in order;
during the downward progression, twenty thousand [moments] are added at each successive stage as they proceed in order.
As the verse states: "In the first transformation, each [level] increases by one thousand, while each [lower level] increases by twenty thousand.
Therefore, is there an increase or decrease in the number of items within the category of quantity?
It is only a measure of equality, not a measure of differentiation, as the verse states: "The measures of equality increase gradually.

Among the six subsequent transformations, they increase by doubling in sequence; that is, they increase by a factor of one [doubling] each time, as the verse states: "In the six subsequent transformations, they increase respectively by doubling the number."

Thus, throughout these seven transformations, there is neither a characteristic of mutual reflection nor a characteristic of concealment; rather, they are established solely as equal portions. As the verse states: "Without the distinctions of interruption or obstruction, they are established solely in relation to their measure."
In this context, one should carefully examine the sequence of the sevenfold transformation as the culmination of the merits.
The *Gambhīra-bījaka-sūtra* states: "Within the inner treasury, there are only three transformations;
seven is the measure, neither more nor less. This is the natural principle (*dharmatā-yukti*), like the 'seven-step snake' or the 'seven-leaf tree'."
"In the beginning, it exists only within the defiled category; subsequently, it exists in both the defiled and the pure categories;

finally, it exists only within the pure category. Thus it is explained at length. Chapter Twenty: The Great Determination on the Fundamental Stage of the King of the *Ṣaḍdhātuvibhaṅga*. Thus has been explained the Great Determination on the Path of the *Ṣaḍdhātuvibhaṅga*. Next, the Great Determination on the Fundamental Stage of the King of the *Ṣaḍdhātuvibhaṅga* shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the essence of this fundamental king, there are three kinds of one hundred transformations.
"The names and sequence are as before; they are equal and without distinction. The commentary states:

Within this fundamental essence of the primary king, there are three kinds of hundredfold transformations of practice. Their names and sequence are as previously explained, for as the verse says: "Within this fundamental essence of the primary king, there are three kinds of hundredfold [transformations]; their names and sequence are as before, equal and without distinction."
What are the characteristics of these three transformations?
The verse says:
Within these three transformations, the first [set] is, respectively, as follows:
Ten thousand times one hundred billion, followed by ninety-nine transformations,
each increasing in double the preceding number, gradually turning in successive order.
The commentary says:
Within the hundredfold gate of faults, from the upper and lower levels, the first transformation increases by ten billion units, proceeding through gradual transitions.
Within the hundredfold gate of merits, from the upper and lower levels, the first transformation increases by one thousand billion units, proceeding through gradual transitions.
Within the hundredfold transformation gates of equal measure, from the upper to the lower, in the first transformation, the number increases by ten billion, progressing gradually in sequence.
As the verse states: "Thus, within these three transformations, in each of the first, there are respectively ten, one hundred, and ten billion."

In the subsequent ninety-nine transformations, each increases by doubling in accordance with its respective order, as stated in the verse: "The subsequent ninety-nine transformations increase by doubling in sequence, turning gradually and in successive order."
The *Mahāsamudragirisvarūpabhūmiprakāra-sūtra* states:
"Within the essence of the Tathāgatagarbha, there are three categories of transmigration, numbering in the hundreds; they proceed without skipping stages, evolving gradually."
"Among these three, the first has little merit and many faults; the middle one has merit and faults in equal measure; and the last has only merit.
Thus it is explained at length.
The Treatise on the Profound Fundamental Text of the Great Totality, Scroll Ten.
The Treatise on the Profound Fundamental Text of the Great Totality, Scroll Eleven.

Chapter Twenty-one: The Great Determination of the Path of the King of the *Ṛṣividyā* Mantras. Thus, having already explained the Great Determination of the Fundamental Stage of the King of the *Ṛṣividyā* Mantras, next shall be explained the Great Determination of the Path of the King of the *Ṛṣividyā* Mantras.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of the fundamental king, there are three kinds of thousandfold transformations.
The names and measures are as previously explained;
each initial transformation increases by one hundred, ten thousand, a million, and ten billion respectively.
Each subsequent transformation multiplies by double the preceding amount; one should observe this with a settled mind.
The treatise states:

Within the section on the path of the fundamental king *Ṣi-van-na*, there are three types of thousandfold transformations in practice; their names and sequence are the same as previously explained, as the verse says: "Within the path of the fundamental king, there are three types of thousandfold transformations, with names and measures as previously stated."

Regarding these three types, in the first transformation, they increase respectively by one hundred billion, one thousand billion, and ten thousand billion; because the measurements of the upper and lower dimensions gradually expand, as the verse states: "In each initial transformation, they increase respectively by hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, and billions."

One should carefully examine and discern how each subsequent transformation increases by doubling in its respective order, as the verse states: "Each subsequent transformation of all [preceding ones] proceeds by doubling in sequence; one who abides in the mind should observe this. Thus it is said.
The *Treatise on the Sūtras* states as follows:
"Within the upper and lower gates of the Tathāgatagarbha-buddha, there are three types of numerical practices, measured by the thousands."
"In this way, these three categories give rise to, increase, expand, and pervade a vast ocean-treasury of Dharma-gates through many billions of turnings.
Thus it is explained at length. 22.

The Great Determination of the Sovereign Heavenly King Mahā-ṛṣi-vana-nāma-mūla-prabhava. The Great Determination of the Sovereign Heavenly King Mahā-ṛṣi-vana-nāma-mūla-prabhava, the twenty-second. Having thus already explained the Great Determination of the Path of the Sovereign King Ṛṣi-vana, next the Great Determination of the Sovereign Heavenly King Mahā-ṛṣi-vana-nāma-mūla-prabhava shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the realm of the Mahārāja deities, there are three kinds of billions of transformations.
The sequence of names is as before; each undergoes its first transformation in order within the ten directions—one, two, three, and ten—whereby the number of world-systems increases.
All subsequent transformations increase by doubling in their respective order.
The Treatise says:

Within the essence of the Mahā-indra Heavenly King, there are three kinds of billions of transformative practices (*bhāvanā*). Their names and sequence are the same as those previously explained, as the verse states: "Within the Mahā-indra Heavenly King, there are three kinds of billions of transformations; their names and sequence are as before."

Regarding these three types [of transformations], in the first transformation they increase respectively by one, ten, and twenty directions; as the verse states: "In each initial transformation, according to the sequence, the number of world-systems increases by ten, twenty, and thirty directions. Thus it is.
All other transformations increase in successive multiples according to their order, as stated in the verse: "All remaining transformations increase in successive multiples."
In the *Sarvākṣaradharmaparivartamahācakra-sūtra*, it is stated:
"Within the stages of the Buddha’s Great Fundamental Treasury King, there are three practices."
What are the three? First, the lower billion-fold revolution; second, the middle billion-fold revolution; and third, the upper billion-fold revolution.

The first practice gives rise to a sea of lower retinues equal in measure to one great world-system; the middle practice gives rise to a sea of simultaneous revolutions equal in measure to two great world-systems; and the final practice gives rise to a sea of upper retinues equal in measure to three great world-systems.
...and so forth, as explained at length.

Chapter Twenty-Three: The Great Determination of the Path of the Single, Pure, and Unadulterated Ground of Great Perfection. Thus, having already explained the Great Determination of Mahādeva, the Original Lord of the Heavenly Kings, we shall now explain the Great Determination of the Path of the Single, Pure, and Unadulterated Ground of Great Perfection.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of merit, there are two thousand five hundred.
Within the ocean of fifty dharma-gates, across the fifty-one stages,
each and every one of them individually possesses all fifty stages. Furthermore, within each and every stage,
there are both essence and characteristics, as well as the fundamental and the derivative.
The number one thousand and two hundred is taught in the Sūtras; together they total twelve thousand.
Taking the number seven hundred and fifty from that total, one should observe them according to the Dharma.
"By such a number, it constitutes the demarcation of the path.
The commentary states:

Within the single category of the path of the Great Perfection (*mahāsandhi*), which is pure and unmixed with any other qualities, there are in total two thousand five hundred and fifty oceans of dharma-gates, which are exceedingly profound and exceedingly vast. As the verse says: "Within the path of qualities, there are two thousand five hundred and fifty oceans of dharma-gates."
For what reason should it be understood that the number is established in this way?
It is because within each of the fifty-one stages, each one individually possesses fifty [factors].
What is the meaning of this?

It refers to the fact that the fifty stages of the mind of faith (*śraddhā-citta*), the fifty stages of the mind of mindfulness (*smṛti-citta*), and so forth, up to the fifty stages of the Tathāgata-bhūmi, each have their own distinct differences. As the verse states: "Within the fifty-one stages, each and every one possesses all fifty stages."
Furthermore, because each and every stage is fully endowed with the four dharmas of nature, characteristics, origin, and culmination, the total number of ten thousand and two hundred is established.
How, then, are these four matters distinguished?

This means that, respectively, they are taught as the inconceivable, taught as the clear and manifest awakening, taught as the cause that can produce growth, and taught as the fruit produced by growth; as the verse says: "Furthermore, within each and every stage, there are essence, characteristics, root, and branch, numbering one thousand and two hundred."
If that is so, how is the textual passage from this region to be interpreted?
It refers to what is stated in the *Vajrabhūmi-ekavyūha-samādhi-sūtra*:

"Within the gateways of the ritual rules for each stage of the auspicious ground—which are unmixed, undisturbed, uniform, identical, neither evil nor afflictive—there are, in total, twelve thousand seven hundred and fifty dharma-gates."

Regarding what is thus stated in that *sūtra*, it is because of the principle of the general and the particular; as the verse says: "In the *sūtra* it is said that the total number is twelve thousand seven hundred and fifty; taking that total fundamental number, one should observe it according to the Dharma. Thus it is.
Now, this path is measured by means of that [number], for there is a distinct dharma-gate;
it takes only this number as its ultimate limit, with no other dharma-gate, as the verse says: "By such a quantity, the boundaries of the path are established."

24. The Great Decisive Analysis on the Section for Clarifying the Separation from Evil within the Mahā-bhūmi of the Single Quality, the Treasury of the Pure and Unmixed Great Perfection Grounds. The Great Decisive Analysis on the Section for Clarifying the Separation from Evil within the Mahā-bhūmi of the Single Quality, the Treasury of the Pure and Unmixed Great Perfection Grounds, Number Twenty-Four. Thus, the Great Decisive Analysis on the Road of the Single Quality, the Pure and Unmixed Great Perfection Grounds, has already been explained; next, the Great Decisive Analysis on the Section for Clarifying the Separation from Evil within the Mahā-bhūmi of the Single Quality, the Treasury of the Pure and Unmixed Great Perfection Grounds, shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the *Mūlabhūmi-vastu-saṃgrahaṇī*, there are one hundred and three million [verses].
Seven thousand five hundred in number, Are the oceans of vast Dharma-gates.
Within each of the stages previously explained, Each one individually encompasses fifty distinct positions; Thus are the Dharma-gates so extensive.
Regarding the four categories of nature, characteristics, origin, and culmination, one should extensively penetrate them by following this analogy.
The Treatise says:

Within the *Mahā-bhūmi-vibhāga-kuśala-dharma-garbha* (The Treasury of the Mahā-bhūmi that is Clear and Free from Evil Elements), there are in total one hundred and three million seven thousand five hundred vast dharma-gate oceans, which are exceedingly profound and all-pervasive. As the verse states: "Within the *Bhūmi-garbha*, there are one hundred and three million seven thousand five hundred vast dharma-gate oceans."
For what reason is the number established in this way?

As previously stated, because within each and every one of all the stages, there are fifty distinct stages subsumed within each respectively; thus, the ocean of dharma-gates is so vast. As stated in the preceding verse, because within each and every stage there are fifty distinct stages subsumed within each respectively, the dharma-gates are thus extensive.

Within the four matters of nature, characteristics, root, and branch, they are matched by analogy; furthermore, as the number increases, they become increasingly superior and vast. One should examine and discern this carefully, for as the verse says: "Nature, characteristics, root, and branch—by analogy with these, one attains broad and thorough penetration."
The Treatise on the Profound Fundamental Text of the Great Primary Ground, Scroll Twelve.
The Treatise on the Profound Fundamental Text of the Great Primary Ground, Scroll Thirteen.

The Great Section on the Foundation of the Grounds, Chapter on the Fulfillment of the Store, Sub-section: The Great Determination of the Path Free from Affliction. The Great Section on the Foundation of the Grounds, Chapter on the Fulfillment of the Store, Sub-section: The Great Determination of the Path Free from Affliction, Number Twenty-five. Having thus explained the Great Determination of the Section on the Clear Departure from Evil within the Singlefold Merit of the Great Section on the Foundation of the Grounds, next shall be explained the Great Determination of the Path Free from Affliction within the Chapter on the Fulfillment of the Store of the Great Section on the Foundation of the Grounds.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the stages and paths of the fundamental level, there are two kinds of gates.
That is to say, there are horizontal and vertical revolutions; these are taken as the measure of the gates.
The treatise says:
Within the section on the Path Free from Affliction in the Mahā-bhūmi-samparigraha-vastu-kośa, there are two gates.

What are the two? First is the gate of horizontal revolution, universal arrival, and simultaneous progression; second is the gate of vertical revolution, non-confusion, and the single path. These are called the two.

These two gates constitute the measure of the gateway, as the verse states: "Within the paths of the fundamental stage, there are two kinds of gates; namely, horizontal transition and vertical transition, which serve as the measure of the gateway."
Furthermore, as for the transverse arrangement of the gates, what is their form?
The verse says:
Within the four types of matters and stages, there are both general and specific [arrangements].
Each increases by ten layers of revolutions; without before or after, they occur simultaneously.
The number of these dharma-gates should be understood by analogy with what precedes.
The treatise says:
What meaning is clarified in this verse?

It is intended to demonstrate that within the four matters of essence, characteristics, root, and branches, each possesses both general and specific positions; in every single position, ten layers of numbers are added respectively, revolving simultaneously without before or after. This is because it represents the form and characteristics of the "transverse revolution, universal arrival, and simultaneous progression" gate. As the verse says: "Within the positions of the four matters, amidst the general and the specific, each increases by ten layers of revolution, without before or after, occurring all at once."

Within this context, the numerical quantity is further increased and surpasses the previous measure; this should be understood through analogy, as the verse states that the numerical measure of these dharma-gates should be understood by analogy with what preceded.
Having thus explained the gate of simultaneous universal pervasion through horizontal transition, next the gate of the single path of vertical transition without admixture shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Among the various stages previously explained, they do not exceed their respective order;
each increases by tenfold transformations, as one clarifies the ultimate state.
The treatise says:

What meaning is clarified by this verse? It is intended to demonstrate that within the general and specific stages previously described, there is no skipping over their respective order; rather, each stage individually increases by tenfold revolutions. Each single matter clarifies and brings another matter to completion, without confusion or synthesis, as they proceed exclusively through a vertical progression of unmixed, singular paths. As the verse states: "Within the various stages previously taught, there is no skipping over the sequence; each increases by tenfold revolutions, for one clarification leads to ultimate completion."
The *Mahāvajraratnarājadharmadhātumudrāgarbhasūtra* states as follows: "Furthermore, Mañjuśrī,
the Chapter on the Path of Jewels proceeds by means of two matters."
What are the two? First, turning in a single sector; second, turning with all sides.
Regarding "a single sector," although the path may be extensive and manifold, it is because one first reaches the ultimate limit of the measure of a single path.
"Regarding 'possessing all aspects,' it is because all paths are traversed simultaneously," as explained at length. 26.

*Mahāratnacakra-rājā-vipula-paripūrṇa-anuttara-bhūmi-bhūmi-mahā-viniścaya-vibhāga*, the twenty-sixth section: "The Great Decision-Making Analysis of the Stages and Sub-stages of the Vast, Perfect, and Unsurpassed Mahāratnacakra-rāja. Thus has been explained the *Mahā-mūla-bhūmi-sampad-piṭaka-avyādhi-mārga-mahā-viniścaya-vibhāga*; next, the *Mahāratnacakra-rājā-vipula-paripūrṇa-anuttara-bhūmi-bhūmi-mahā-viniścaya-vibhāga* shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Because the general and the particular are inexhaustible, the essence of the fundamental dharma is established.
The Commentary says:
What meaning is clarified in this verse?

It is intended to demonstrate that within the essence of the fundamental dharma (mūladharma), the general encompasses the particular, the particular encompasses the general, the general encompasses the general, and the particular encompasses the particular; thus, the relationship between the encompassing and the encompassed is inexhaustible. Because the ocean of dharma-gates is profoundly deep and vast, its principles and expressions are all-pervasive and perfect, reaching ultimate mastery—as the verse states: "Because the general and the particular are inexhaustible, the essence of the fundamental dharma is established."
In the *Mahāyāna Akṣayamati-kṣitigarbha-anuttara-paramārtha-acintya-citta-bhūmi-parivarta-śāstra-sūtra*, it is stated as follows:

“Within the ocean of jewel mountains, the similar classes are inexhaustible and the distinct classes are inexhaustible; they are fully perfected, without end, without beginning or end, without limit, and without boundary; they possess both vast characteristics and minute characteristics.”
...and so forth, as explained at length.

Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Great Decisive Analysis of the Inauspicious Paths of the Various Categories of the Stages of Bondage (*Bandhana-bhūmi-prakāra-aśubha-mārga-mahā-viniścaya*). Thus has been explained the Great Decisive Analysis of the Vast, Perfect, and Unsurpassed Stages of the Great Jewel-Wheel King (*Mahā-ratna-cakra-rāja*). Next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Inauspicious Paths of the Various Categories of the Stages of Bondage shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of bondage, there is also the stage of the vajra.
Based on the stages, the characteristics of transformation are established; there are thus four kinds of phenomena:
namely, the agent, the object, the obscuration, and the fruit.
These four kinds of phenomena are all of a conditioned nature; they should be observed according to the Dharma.
The Treatise says:

Within the section on the paths of inauspiciousness categorized by their respective stages and types of bondage, there are likewise fifty-one adamantine positions (*vajrapada*). Based on these various positions, the establishment of the characteristics of transformation involves four kinds of dharmas.

What are the four? First, the phenomena of the wisdom that realizes; second, the principles of what is realized; third, the phenomena that constitute obstacles; and fourth, the phenomena of the fruit attained through realization. These are called the four.

These four dharmas are all conditioned (*saṃskṛta*) in measure; they should be carefully examined and discerned. As the verse says: "Within the path of bondage, there is also the stage of the vajra; based on these stages, the characteristics of transformation are established, consisting of four kinds of dharmas—namely, the subject, the object, the obscuration, and the fruit. These four kinds of dharmas are all conditioned in measure; they should be observed according to the Dharma. Thus it is said.
How many instances are there for each of these four dharmas?
How do their transformations correspond?
The verse says:
Each possesses two kinds of dharmas, namely the fundamental and the initial, as well as essence and appearance;
there are also arising and ceasing, as well as increase and decrease, while the aspect of transformation pertains only to the progressively higher stages.
The treatise says:
Within each of the four kinds of dharmas, there are two types.
What are these two knowledges?
First is the primordial, ancient virtue-wisdom; second is the newly arisen virtue-wisdom. These are called the two.
What are the two principles?
First, the principle of the reality of essence; second, the principle of the reality of characteristics—these are called the two.
What are the two obstacles?
The first is the fundamental arising and the obstruction of fundamental arising; the second is the fundamental cessation and the obstruction of fundamental cessation—these are called the two.
What are the two fruits?
The first is the fruit of increasing merit and virtue; the second is the fruit of diminishing faults and afflictions—these are called the two.
As the verse states: "Each possesses two kinds of dharmas, namely the fundamental and the initial aspects of essence and characteristic, as well as arising-and-ceasing and increasing-and-decreasing.
Because the aspect of transformation through cultivation is exclusively superior-to-the-superior, as the verse says: "The aspect of transformation is exclusively superior-to-the-superior."
Regarding the distinctions between the obstacles (*āvaraṇa*), their remedies (*pratipakṣa*), the realization (*sākṣātkriyā*), and the fruits (*phala*), what are their characteristics?
The verse says:
The fundamental [nature] and arising are contrasted with increase; The initial [state] and cessation are contrasted with decrease.
"From the many, one also attains thorough understanding; one should observe according to the Dharma.
The commentary states:

The fundamental, primordial nature of wisdom and virtue eliminates the obstacles of both the original and the produced, realizes the true principle of the existence of the essence, and accomplishes the increase of the fruits of merit, as the verse says: "The original, the produced, the essence, and the increase are in correspondence."

Now, having initiated the cultivation of wisdom and virtue, one eliminates and extinguishes the fundamental obstructions; one realizes the true principle of the existence of characteristics and achieves the fruit that subdues the faults of diminution, as the verse says: "The antidote, extinction, characteristic, diminution, and opposition."
These four dharmas are fully present within the fifty-one types of the stage of true gold; one should examine and discern them carefully:
do they function solely as a single transformation, or do they transform together?
Because both seeds undergo transformation, as the verse states: "From the predominant [seed], there is also thorough comprehension; one should observe this according to the Dharma.
What are the characteristics of the functional distinctions between the two obstacles—arising and cessation?
The verse says:
When the original master arises and ceases, it is because there is a superior arising and a superior cessation.
The commentary says:

The emergence of meritorious roots of goodness and the emergence of increasingly superior remedies occur because these superior remedies act as counteragents to cessation; as the verse says: "When the original master arises and ceases, there is the arising and ceasing of that which is superior. Thus it is.
In the *Mahāvajraśaila-ratnasāgara-parṣad-sūtra*, it is said:
"Furthermore, Mañjuśrī! Regarding what you previously asked:
'What is meant by the single path, the single type, and the primary gateway of the impermanence of all phenomena? "
Because there are four kinds of impermanence, I have made this proclamation.

What are these four? First, the impermanence of wisdom; second, the impermanence of principle; third, the impermanence of impermanence; and fourth, the impermanence of the supreme fruit. These are called the four.
Mañjuśrī! To say that wisdom is impermanent is because it severs the afflictions.
To say that principle is impermanent is because it is that which is realized by wisdom.
"Regarding the statement 'the impermanent is impermanent,' it is because it has been severed and eliminated.
Regarding the statement 'the effect is impermanent,' it is because it depends upon the power of causes.
Thus it is explained at length.

28. The Great Decisive Analysis of the Chapter on the Great *Vajra* of the Natural Sovereign King of the Grounds of Bondage. Thus, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Chapter on the Inauspicious Paths of the Categories of the Grounds of Bondage has already been explained. Next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Chapter on the Great *Vajra* of the Natural Sovereign King of the Grounds of Bondage shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the naturally existing fundamental king, there are both conditioned and unconditioned phenomena.
"Perfectly complete and revolving; herein are both the upper and the lower.
The commentary states:
Within the section on the Mahābija, the Sovereign King of Naturalness, there are two revolutions.

What are these two? First, the transformation of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*); second, the transformation of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). These are called the two, as the verse states: "Within the naturally sovereign fundamental source, the conditioned and unconditioned dharmas transform in complete and perfect abundance."
There are also two types of turning. What are these two?
First, upward turning; second, downward turning. These are called the two, as stated in the verse: "In this, both upward and downward are complete."
How many are there for each of the conditioned and the unconditioned?
How do their upper and lower transitions correspond?
The verse says:
The unconditioned is only one; the conditioned is of two kinds.
Accordingly, they are the ultimate reality, the fundamental, and the initial;
The superior and inferior unconditioned are primary, Giving rise to the two kinds of conditioned phenomena, Which evolve into ever-greater excellence and vastness.
The treatise states:
The unconditioned has one [nature], while the conditioned has two.

The first refers to its being substantial; the second refers to its being both fundamental and derivative. As the verse says: "The unconditioned has only one, and the conditioned has two kinds; respectively, these are the substantial, the fundamental, and the derivative."
Regarding these three dharmas, within the fifty-one stages of the Vajra-position, they increase merit both upward and downward.
What is the manner of this transformation?

It means that during the upward progression, each and every stage is presided over by unconditioned dharmas, and each respectively gives rise to and increases ten thousand fundamental and initial pure, wondrous, and awakened wisdoms.
During that period of descent, within each and every stage, two hundred million fundamental and initial pure, wondrous, and awakened wisdoms are fully perfected, brought forth, and increased.

In this way, and in this way, from the upper and lower realms down to the smallest immeasurable [unit], it is as stated regarding the original existence of its retinue; as the verse says: "Above and below there is no master; it gives rise to the two conditioned existences, revolving with ever-increasing vastness."
One should understand that the numbers increase according to their respective order.
In the *Sūtra on the Stages of the Sections* (*Pin-di-jing-lun-xu-duo-luo*), it is stated:

"Within the ocean of the fundamental king of the world-treasury stage (*loka-garbha-bhūmi-mūla-rāja-sāgara*), the qualities of impermanence are numerous and incalculable, while the qualities of permanence are few in number; therefore, it is called the 'world-treasury stage.'"
...and so on, as explained at length.

The Great Determination Section on the Path of Unobstructed and Unimpeded Co-arising in the Ground of Vast Transformation of the Natural Sovereign Source. The Great Determination Section on the Ground of Vast Transformation of the Natural Sovereign Source, the Path of Unobstructed and Unimpeded Co-arising, is the twenty-ninth. Thus has been explained the Great Determination Section on the Chapter of the Mahā-vigraha, the Natural Sovereign Source of each Ground within the Grounds of Bondage. Next, the Great Determination Section on the Path of Unobstructed and Unimpeded Co-arising in the Ground of Vast Transformation of the Natural Sovereign Source shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of the fundamental king, it evolves gradually according to its positions.

One primary [element] gives rise to two companions; because they reach the middle and are immeasurable, their numerical transformations are all pervasive. One should observe them according to the Dharma.
The Commentary says:

Within the section on the path of simultaneous practice that is unobstructed and unhindered during the stage of the vast transformation of the sovereign of nature, one proceeds by gradually turning upward and downward according to the sequence of the fifty-one stages.

The unconditioned primary gives rise to two conditioned factors, whether superior or inferior, increasing through immeasurable numbers in the middle, until they reach the immeasurable transformations in the middle.

As the verse says: "On the path of the primary king, proceeding gradually according to its positions, one lord gives birth to two companions; because they reach the immeasurable in the middle, all numerical transformations are fully pervasive; this should be observed in accordance with the Dharma. Thus it is said.
The *Sūtra on the Chapter of the Flower of the Sect* states:

"Within the ocean of the treasury of practices (*caryā-kośa-samudra*), there is one quality of permanence, the number of which is immeasurable; within the ocean of the treasury of practices, there are two categories of impermanent qualities, the number of which is immeasurable, as are those that ascend and those that descend."
"...and so forth, as explained at length. 30.

The Great Decisive Analysis of the Ocean of the Inexhaustible Sea of the Mountain King Accompanied by the Most Utterly Vast [Qualities], Part Thirty. Thus has been explained the Great Decisive Analysis of the Road Accompanied by Unobstructed and Unimpeded [Wisdom] in the Stage of the Vast Transformation of the Spontaneous Fundamental King. Next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Ocean of the Inexhaustible Sea of the Mountain King Accompanied by the Most Utterly Vast [Qualities] shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the ocean of inexhaustible oceans, it evolves gradually according to its stages.

One primary [element] gives rise to two companions; because they reach the state of the great and the immeasurable, their enumeration and transformations follow the previous examples, which one should extensively master and penetrate.
The treatise says:

Within the inexhaustible ocean of the ocean-treasury, based upon the fifty-one stages, proceeding in their respective order both upward and downward, the Unconditioned Lord of Dharmas gives birth to and increases the two types of conditioned dharmas, expanding them to immeasurable numbers until they reach the state of Great Immeasurability.

As the verse says: "Within the ocean of inexhaustible oceans, they evolve gradually according to their stages; from one primary, two companions arise, until reaching the great and the immeasurable. Their numbers and transformations follow the preceding examples; one should extensively master them. Thus it is said.
In that sūtra, it is stated as follows:
"Within the ocean of the Constant Mountain King, there are three kinds of great immeasurables.
What are these three?"
"First, the eternally great immeasurable; second, the non-eternally great immeasurable; third, the transformationally great immeasurable.
Thus it is explained at length.

The Great Decisive Analysis of the Path of Pure Liberation in the Stage of Deliverance from Bondage. Thus, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Infinite Ocean of the Mountain King, accompanied by the Most Vast [Qualities], has been explained. Next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Path of Pure Liberation in the Stage of Deliverance from Bondage shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of liberation, there are twenty unconditioned phenomena.
That is to say, the ten emptinesses and the ten existences—such non-conditioned phenomena (asaṃskṛta) are all fully present within the fifty-one stages.
Based on these stages, the turning [of the wheel] is established; there are two types: the progressive and the leap-over.
The Treatise states:

Within the stage of liberation from bondage, which consists of the path of pure and white deliverance, there are twenty unconditioned and eternal dharmas; namely, the ten kinds of emptiness and the ten kinds of unconditioned existence, each being distinct.

What are the ten unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) emptinesses? First, the unconditioned emptiness of the vast, natural, and eternally abiding space that is free from fabrication; second, the unconditioned emptiness of the shadow of great space; third, the unconditioned emptiness of the shadow of the shadow of space; fourth, the unconditioned emptiness of the non-existence resulting from the destruction of shadows; fifth, the unconditioned emptiness of the mutual negation of both space and emptiness; sixth, the unconditioned emptiness that transcends words and cuts off speech; seventh, the unconditioned emptiness of the ultimate transcendence and detachment; eighth, the unconditioned emptiness of the mind’s liberation through ultimate transcendence and detachment; ninth, the unconditioned emptiness of the ultimate exhaustion of all exhaustion; tenth, the unconditioned emptiness of the great emptiness and the emptiness of the emptiness of the great emptiness, which is without obstruction or hindrance. These are called the ten.
What are the ten unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta*) that exist?
First, the unconditioned phenomenon of the certainty and eternal abiding of all verbal expressions, which is indestructible and not empty;
second, the unconditioned phenomenon of the certainty and eternal abiding of all mental consciousnesses, which is indestructible and not empty; third, all primary elements (*mahābhūta*).

1. That which is definitively permanent, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned; 2. That which is all-inclusive, neither definitive nor permanent, yet indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned;

3. That which is all-inclusive, definitively permanent, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned; 4. That which is all-inclusive, neither definitive nor permanent, yet indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned;

5. That which is all-existent, substantial, definitively permanent, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned; 6. That which is the Great Nature of all things, definitively permanent, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned.
Seventh, all that is presently luminous is definitively eternally abiding, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned;
eighth, all that has names is definitively eternally abiding, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned;
ninth, all that is nameless is definitively eternally abiding, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned; tenth, the vast and perfect self-...
The nature is fundamentally endowed with all seeds, which are determinate, eternally abiding, indestructible, non-empty, and unconditioned;
these are called the ten.
As the verse says: "Within the path of liberation, there are twenty unconditioned phenomena, namely ten emptinesses and ten existences. Thus it is said.

These twenty kinds of unconditioned phenomena (asaṃskṛta-dharma) function in their complete perfection, without deficiency, throughout the fifty-one stages of the vajra-position; as the verse states: "Thus all these unconditioned phenomena are fully present within the fifty-one stages."
Based on these twenty unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) states, there are two kinds of modes for establishing the manifestation of transformation (*pariṇāma*) across the fifty-one stages.

What are these two? First, the gate of mutual inclusion without obstruction; second, the gate of sequential, disordered, and transcendent transformation. These are the two, as the verse says: "Based on the dharmas and stages, the establishment of transformation has two aspects: mutual inclusion and transcendence."
Furthermore, what are the characteristics of the gate of mutual inclusion without obstruction?
The verse says:
Each of the twenty dharmas individually includes each of the subsequent twenty.
The fifty-one kinds of stages, each and every one of them, encompass all fifty-one stages; they are also encompassed by their mutual opposition.
For these reasons, the name "repeatedly layered" is established.
The Commentary says:
What is meant by the "characteristic of the gate of successive layers"?
It refers to the fact that it encompasses all.
How are they subsumed?

It means that the twenty kinds of unconditioned, eternal dharmas are fully possessed through faith; each and every one of them individually subsumes the twenty kinds of unconditioned dharmas belonging to all subsequent stages.
As it is said regarding the stage of faith, so it is for the other stages as well; for as the verse states: "Each of the twenty dharmas individually encompasses the subsequent twenty.
Thus, each of the fifty-one stages encompasses all fifty-one without obstruction, as the verse states: "Each and every one of the fifty-one stages encompasses all fifty-one stages."
Furthermore, each individual dharma encompasses all stages, and each stage likewise encompasses all dharmas without obstruction, as the verse states: "And these are mutually inclusive."

Because these two types of inclusive gateways are employed, the name "repeatedly layered" (*chong-chong*) is established, as the verse states: "For this reason and condition, the name 'repeatedly layered' is established."
Thus has been explained the gate of mutual inclusion without obstruction; next, the gate of successive, disordered progression and transcendence shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within these fifty-one stages, each one passes through fifty [sub-stages],
gradually increasing the number of dharmas as they revolve extensively and universally.
The treatise says:
What meaning is clarified in this verse?

It is intended to demonstrate that within the fifty-one stages of the vajra-position, one may take faith as the starting point and pass through fifty stages; or take the stage of "abiding in the resolve for enlightenment" (cittotpāda-vihāra) as the starting point and pass through fifty stages; and so on, even taking the ultimate stage (nisthā-bhūmi) as the starting point and passing through fifty stages.

If in the first turning there is a progression through forty-one hundred numerical dharma-positions, and in the second turning there is a progression through eighty-two hundred numerical dharma-positions, this continues until the final stage.

As the verse states: "Within the fifty-one stages, each undergoes fifty [transformations]; gradually increasing the number of dharmas, they revolve extensively and universally. The *Skandha-Parvatarāja-prakāra-sūtra* says:
"Within the gate of the unbreakable stages, there are numerous jewels of tranquility, and numerous jewels of empty tranquility."

If there are practitioners who enter this gateway, they will penetrate the unconditioned Great Way of all phenomena; being without obstruction and without doubt or fear, their minds will attain mastery, remaining forever in definitive great peace and bliss, gradually increasing the ocean of constant merit.
...and so forth, as explained at length.

The Great Decisive Analysis of the Unimpeded Mastery of the Fundamental Grounds of the Mountain King of Liberation, Part Thirty-Two. Thus has been explained the Great Decisive Analysis of the Path of Pure Liberation from the Ground of Deliverance from Bondage; next, the Great Decisive Analysis of the Unimpeded Mastery of the Fundamental Grounds of the Mountain King of Liberation shall be explained.
What are their characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the fundamental king of mountains, emptiness and existence give rise to one another.
"Because all phenomena arise from one another, they increase, become more excellent, and expand further.
The commentary asks:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?

In order to manifest that each of the ten unconditioned dharmas of emptiness gives rise to ten unconditioned dharmas of existence and permanence, and each of the ten unconditioned dharmas of existence and permanence gives rise to ten unconditioned dharmas of emptiness and permanence.

Each of the fifty-one positions gives rise to fifty others through various gateways such as the "mutual dependence" (zhongchong), revolving in a vast and perfect manner. As the verse states: "Within the fundamental mountain king, emptiness and existence give birth to one another; because all positions give birth to one another, they revolve with ever-increasing vastness."
The *Mahāyānasamudra-sūtra* states: "Within the ocean of liberation, there are both those with existence and emptiness, as well as those with emptiness and existence; their number is vast."

Thus, this emptiness and existence are exclusively of the nature of eternal cessation rather than being subject to non-eternal measures; they are exclusively of the category of merit rather than the category of faults. Therefore, it is called the ocean-treasury of liberation.
...and so forth, as explained at length.
*The Great Treatise on the Profound Source of the Fundamental Ground*, Fascicle 16;
*The Great Treatise on the Profound Source of the Fundamental Ground*, Fascicle 17.
Composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;
translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. 33.

The Great Path of the King of Mountains of Liberation: The Great Section on Decisive Discrimination. Thus has been explained the Great Section on Decisive Discrimination concerning the Unobstructed Sovereignty of Each Ground within the Fundamental Grounds of the King of Mountains of Liberation. Next, the Great Section on Decisive Discrimination concerning the Great Path of the King of Mountains of Liberation shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the road of the King of Mountains, according to the measurements previously described.
Increasing emptiness within emptiness and existence within existence, they arise with ever-increasing excellence at each stage.
The commentary says:
Within the great royal road of the mountain king of liberation, there are three turnings.
What are the three?
First is the transformation of emptiness within emptiness, because each of the ten unconditioned states of emptiness gives rise to ten states of emptiness;
second is the transformation of existence within existence, because each of the ten unconditioned states of existence gives rise to ten states of existence.
Third is transformation at each stage, because within each of the fifty-one stages, all fifty [aspects] arise individually.
These are the three. This is because they arise from their own characteristics and not from the characteristics of others.

As the verse says: "Within the path of the King of Mountains, within the previously explained measures, the stages of emptiness-of-emptiness and existence-of-existence arise, each becoming increasingly superior.
One should extensively master the various other gateways through which these numbers increase progressively.

34. The Great Determination of the Great Mountain King of the Ocean of Vast and Inexhaustible Liberations. Thus has been explained the Great Determination of the Great Highway of the Mountain King of Liberation; next, the Great Determination of the Great Mountain King of the Ocean of Vast and Inexhaustible Liberations shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Because the various transformations previously described are without end.
The Commentary states:
What meaning is clarified in this verse?

It is intended to demonstrate that the production of emptiness from itself is inexhaustible, the production of emptiness from other forms of emptiness is inexhaustible, and the production of emptiness from all existents is inexhaustible.

Existence is likewise inexhaustible, and its positions are likewise inexhaustible; they revolve in infinite layers and turn without end. Having no boundaries and no beginning or end, they proceed with profound depth, pervasive universality, and vast expansion—this is because it is the essence, nature, and function of the sovereign, unimpeded King of Mountains within the ocean of liberation.
As the verse says: "Because the various revolutions previously described are without end.
Thus ends the seventeenth fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-tattvasamgraha-nirdeśa-śāstra*;
[beginning] the eighteenth fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-tattvasamgraha-nirdeśa-śāstra*.
Composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;
translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. 35.

The Great Determination of the Path of the King of the Treasury of the Great Void-Dust Ocean (Mahā-śūnyaraja-samudra-garbha-rāja-mārga-mahā-viniścaya). The Great Determination of the Path of the King of the Treasury of the Great Void-Dust Ocean, the thirty-fifth [chapter], is as follows: Having already explained the Great Determination of the Great Mountain King of the Ocean of Vast and Inexhaustible Liberation, one shall now explain the Great Determination of the Path of the King of the Treasury of the Great Void-Dust Ocean.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the path of the Ocean King, one is fully endowed with the hundred sovereign powers.
For these reasons, the name "Ocean King" was established.
The commentary says:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?
This is because he wishes to demonstrate that within the treasury of the Ocean King there is no separate dharma, but only sovereign mastery.
How many kinds of mastery are there?
It is said there are one hundred kinds.
What are the hundred?

First is mastery over time: the thirty-two factors may evolve simultaneously, or they may evolve at different times; they may evolve during the time of non-evolution, or they may evolve during the time of evolution; they may evolve in distant time, or they may evolve in proximate time, and so on, up to the infinite.
Second is mastery over location, because it operates within locations such as unity and difference, up to being immeasurable.
Third is mastery over things, because it functions as identity, difference, and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Fourth is mastery over pervasiveness, meaning there is nothing to which it does not penetrate, and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Fifth is mastery over size, meaning from the extremely heavy to the extremely minute, and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Sixth is mastery over existence and non-existence, such as manifesting and concealing oneself, and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Seventh is mastery over stillness and movement, such as remaining in meditative concentration or emerging from it, and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Eighth is profound mastery, because of inconceivable matters and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Ninth is mastery over non-mastery, because of contrary matters and so forth, up to being immeasurable.
Tenth is unimpeded mastery, because it encompasses all matters—whether contrary or conformable—and extends even to the immeasurable.
Furthermore, from the mastery of mastery up to the hundredth mastery, including the mastery of inexhaustibility and so forth, all are entirely masterful, extending even to the immeasurable.

As previously stated, these thirty-two qualities function with such sovereign perfection, completeness, and absence of deficiency; for this reason, the name "Sāgararāja" (Ocean King) is established, which should be carefully examined and discerned.
As the verse states: "Within the path of the Ocean King, he is endowed with a hundred sovereign powers; for this reason, the name 'Ocean King' is established.
Thus it is said in the *Buddhāvatamsaka Sūtra*:

"In the first extensive section on the gateway of the great ocean, if explained in detail, there are as many sovereign powers as there are atoms in a world-system of the ten directions; if explained briefly, there are one hundred sovereign powers."
"...and so forth, as explained at length. 36.

The Great Inconceivable, Multi-layered, Incommensurable *Aśvabhū* Root King, Great Section of Determination (*Mahā-viniścaya*). Thus, the Great Section of Determination on the Path of the King of the Treasury of the Ocean of Great Empty Dusts has been explained; next, the Great Inconceivable, Multi-layered, Incommensurable *Aśvabhū* Root King, Great Section of Determination shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
Within the *Aśvaghosa-mūla-śāstra*, there are [teachings] as numerous as the atoms of the ten directions.
The amount of dust in the emptiness of the ten directions, And the ocean of the thirty-three dharmas.
The commentary asks:
What meaning is clarified by this verse?

It is because he wishes to manifest and demonstrate the thirty-three oceans of dharmas, as numerous as the atoms in the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in the spaces of the ten directions, and as numerous as the atoms in the worlds of the ten directions—all of which are fully perfected within the ocean of the Aśvaghosa-sūtra.

As stated in the verse: "Within the *Aśvabhū* Root King [Sūtra], there are as many dharmas as there are atoms in the ten directions, as many as there are atoms in the space of the ten directions, and an ocean of thirty-three dharmas.
Thus it is said in the *Aśvabhū-mūla-sūtra*:
"At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:"
"By means of my threefold penetrating wisdom, I have thoroughly realized all dharmas, being without obstruction or deficiency.

Yet there remains one ocean that is inconceivable, utterly inconceivable, and cannot be fully fathomed: namely, the Ocean-Treasury of Infinite Sovereignty, which is the perfect and sovereign nature-virtue of the fundamental source of empty dust."
...and so on, as explained at length.
