The Great Section of Definitive Analysis on the Measurement of Merit, the Praise of Faithful Practice, and the Manifestation of Benefits. Thus has been explained the Great Section of Definitive Analysis on the Sovereign King Aśvabhū, which is immensely inconceivable and of a magnitude beyond all measure. Next, the Great Section of Definitive Analysis on the Measurement of Merit, the Praise of Faithful Practice, and the Manifestation of Benefits shall be explained.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
It is like a mass of blazing fire; though there be places extremely far away, [it reaches them].
By the power of its radiance, it can dispel the darkness of distant lands;
this profound *Mūlamadhyamaka-kārikā* is likewise so.
Should there be any class of sentient beings dwelling together within the same world, [it shall illuminate them all].
Although they have not yet attained the vision of the learner,
they can break through the distant darkness of sentient beings’ mental states;
causing them to attain the light of awakening and knowledge, they subdue their defilements according to their respective capacities.
Just as when there is a great mass of blazing fire, the closer one approaches it,
the more its radiance becomes clearly manifest, and the more it increases in its power to destroy darkness; so too is this *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā*.
If there are classes of sentient beings dwelling together in the same land,
even those who have not yet attained the vision of the training,
may this light of the fire of this treatise remove their ignorance and cause it to become increasingly clear.
Just as when one approaches a great mass of blazing fire,
its radiant brilliance increases all the more;
this *Mūlamadhyamaka-kārikā* is likewise so.
If there are classes of sentient beings dwelling together in the same city, though they have not yet attained the vision of the training,
the light of this treatise’s fire will remove their ignorance,
becoming clearer and clearer as it progresses.
As one draws closer to that place, the radiance increases layer upon layer,
and its warmth warms the body;
this *Xuanwen benlun* is likewise so.
If there are classes of sentient beings dwelling together as one family, even if they have not yet attained the vision of the training;
by means of the brilliant light of this treatise, their mental delusions are removed and their bodies protected,
as it increases more and more.
Having obtained that great mass of fire, this person then attains six kinds of great benefits: namely, being able to ward off the cold,
being able to ripen provisions, and not being harmed by venomous insects and the like.
It dispels darkness and is ever-luminous; it bestows universally upon those who request it, burning away filth and excrement.
This *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* is likewise so.
Upon obtaining this profound treatise, a person immediately attains six kinds of great benefits: namely, restraining the army of afflictions,
accomplishing the category of merit, and not entering the ranks of demonic hordes.
Breaking through the categories of ignorance, the wisdom of *prajñā* manifests before one;
to sentient beings who come to beg for the impoverished wealth of the Buddha-dharma,
one bestows it universally according to their needs, burning away the filth of afflictions.
For example, there is a wondrous flower growing in a deep pool of water called the blue lotus;
if someone were to behold the appearance of this lotus for a single moment,
[the merit would endure] for one hundred and seven days.
The faculty of the eye is pure and clear, Never clouded or turbid throughout the day;
This *Mūlamadhyamaka-kārikā* is likewise so.
If there are sentient beings Who, though they do not know this treatise,
The great ocean of words and meanings— by beholding this treatise with one's own eyes,
the faculty of sight becomes pure, and one sees all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
this is the eye of skillful means.
Suspended from the crown of the Kalpavṛkṣa tree is one named Wondrous Sound Awakening;
when the immeasurable daughters of the gods hear the sound of this drum,
for twenty-one days their faculty of hearing becomes clear and swift.
There is no obstruction or separation;
it is likewise so: if there are any classes of sentient beings who, though they do not understand the words and their meanings, hear this treatise with their ears.
His faculty of hearing is pure, hearing the Brahma-sounds of all Buddhas;
he possesses the ear of skillful means.
Born upon the summit of the Snowy Mountains, his name is Constant Supreme Flavor.
If someone takes this medicine and applies it to the root of the tongue,
their body will emit an exceedingly fragrant scent; even without consuming food or drink,
their life will be extremely long, and they shall also soar through the void.
This *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* is likewise so:
if there are any classes of sentient beings who [encounter] even a single word, a single verse,
a single line, or even a single section of definitive analysis within this treatise, [they shall attain liberation].
If one recites even the length of a single fascicle with the tongue,
though one may not understand its meaning, one shall obtain the merit of reciting all the oceans of *sūtras*.
For example, there was a bodhisattva named Acintya, a possessor of great power and liberation;
because this mahāsattva possessed mastery over supernormal powers, in all that he undertook—
All are without obstruction, manifesting before one according to need;
this *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* is likewise so:
if there are sentient beings who contemplate and penetrate its principles, [they shall attain liberation].
Awakening to the explanations beneath the words, one penetrates all phenomena without any obstruction, clearly awakening to each and every one.
It is like a divine king, named Great Peace and Bliss, who—
Just as some require small offerings to worship this divine king,
so that he may bring forth the treasury of the seven jewels and grant them great peace and happiness;
so too is it with this *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā*.
If there should be a man or woman who diligently receives, takes up,

reads, and recites this *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā*, and if someone possessing even slight means should single-mindedly provide for such a person, they shall immediately attain that which is inexhaustible.
The jewels of merit and wisdom possess a mind free from doubt or fear.
It is like a wondrous incense called "Pervasive Fragrance":
if someone carries this incense and travels to distant lands, [its scent spreads everywhere].
Wherever it passes through, for the interval of seven times seven days, its fragrance will not fade;
this *Xuanwen Benlun* is likewise so. Should there be any man or woman, [who encounters it...]
Bearing this treatise upon their shoulders, they shall travel to distant lands;
as if crossing the waters of the great ocean, all sentient beings therein shall obtain great benefit, as if crossing over mountains, wilds, and the like.
All sentient beings likewise obtain great benefit.
It is like a wondrous jewel named Cintāmaṇi;
wherever this jewel dwells, there are immeasurable retinues of gems.
Surrounding them on all sides;
likewise, wherever they dwell, throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
there are great spirit-kings as numerous as the atoms of dust.
Each and every one of these great divine kings, leading retinues of deities as numerous as the atoms of the worlds of the ten directions, shall protect this pearl of a treatise.
When the True Dharma is about to perish, they shall reduce it to fine dust and scatter it to ruin.
All the various kings of gods, raising their voices in loud weeping,
shall go wherever the dust settles and constantly provide protection.
Such is the number of deities who will protect those who uphold this treatise.
Whether in life or after death, one is never separated from protection;
though merit is immeasurable, it is briefly explained thus.

(38) The Great Section on the Definitive Analysis of the Measurement of Faults, the Reproach of Slander, and the Demonstration of Karmic Offenses (The Thirty-eighth). Thus, having already explained the Great Section on the Definitive Analysis of the Measurement of Merit, the Praise of Faithful Practice, and the Demonstration of Benefits, next shall be explained the Great Section on the Definitive Analysis of the Measurement of Faults, the Reproach of Slander, and the Demonstration of Karmic Offenses.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
For example, there is a mountain named Ratnacakra-uttara (Supreme Jewel Wheel).
This mountain is endowed with the seven treasures, which are inexhaustible;
there are countless and boundless varieties of those who, being poor, seek such jewels.
There is a pearl capable of restraining these treasures, named *Cūḍāmaṇi-vaidūrya*.
If a person possesses this jewel, they can obtain the seven treasures,
remain far removed from the suffering of poverty, and attain great peace and happiness;
if a person lacks this jewel, they cannot guard their treasures.
Throughout the entire day, he was unable to find it.
When asked why this was so, [he replied:
"If no person comes seeking the jewel, one sees only tigers, wolves, and bears."
Along with red snakes and blue snakes, and various kinds of venomous insects, he never sees the precious treasure.
His mind is filled with extreme doubt and fear; frantic and disordered, he runs about.
Even until death and extinction,
that person seeking the treasure, due to meager merit and heavy transgressions,
will ultimately be unable to see or obtain it.
Those whose roots of goodness are profound, holding the pearl of firm faith,
enter the deep ocean of the Mahāyāna to retrieve the jewels of merit and escape the suffering wheel of birth and death.
Having encountered this most profound treatise, because they lack genuine faith, they misinterpret the authentic teaching as false;
thus they suffer in the cycle of rebirth for an indefinite time.
It is like one born blind who, having obtained exquisite ornaments, [cannot see them].
There is no cause for joy;
though they may obtain profound treatises, because their ignorance is extreme,
they do not perceive the world-transcending treasure and lack any mind for study.
Just as a dragon dwelling in a well, having followed the flowing water to the ocean,
dies of slander because of its great delusion and great confusion;
so too is the foolish person, who stubbornly clings to what they themselves have practiced.
Fixed in a single state without shifting, Upon hearing the unprecedented Dharma,
they become greatly deluded and deeply disturbed; Because they slander its vastness,
they fall into the evil realms, With no time of escape in sight.
If there are beings who, upon seeing or hearing this discourse on the teaching,
do not believe it but instead slander it— such persons then slander all Buddhas of the three periods of time and the treasuries of all dharmas of the three periods of time.
The oceans of the Sangha throughout the three periods of time— the measure of the sins committed by this person is immeasurable and beyond counting; one cannot know their limit.
Equal in number to the atoms of the worlds of the ten directions, are the Buddhas and the great Bodhisattvas.
All appearing simultaneously, they proclaim such an ocean-like gateway of Dharma;
yet though they devote themselves solely to teaching this person for immeasurable eons, they ultimately cannot convert them.
Question: Why is this so? Because it is only this Dharma that is proclaimed, for there is no other distinct path.
The Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in the realms of the ten directions, [rely upon it].
By means of great supernormal power, observing the limits of future distant eons,
there is no time for the realization of the path of awakening.
If one asks why this is so:
The Great Vajra Rite cannot reach the shore of Great Nirvāṇa;
such a thing is impossible.
Therefore, all practitioners, through diligent cultivation of skillful means, should contemplate this ocean of dharmas.
Unable to reach its source, they give rise to a mind of false slander;
falling into the evil realms, there will be no time of escape.
One must certainly not do this; one must certainly not do this.
Although karmic offenses are immeasurable, they have been briefly explained in this manner.

39. The Great Section on the Definitive Establishment and Dispelling of Doubts to Generate Faith by Revealing the Original Cause. Thus, having already explained the Great Section on the Definitive Establishment of Faults through the Comparison of Sins, the Reprimand of Slander, and the Revelation of Karmic Offenses, next we shall explain the Great Section on the Definitive Establishment and Dispelling of Doubts to Generate Faith by Revealing the Original Cause.
What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
"In the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas, I followed the World-Honored One in practicing the bodhisattva path."
At one time, the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Suvarṇavālukā, where the king was named Ratnasuvarṇacakravartigarbha.
This great king possessed thirty billion male and female servants,
sixty billion magnificent white horses, and inexhaustible treasures such as gold and silver.
There was a most lowly slave named Changxin; therein the Great King addressed Changxin:
"Receive these six billion horses and guard them without fail, ensuring they suffer no injury."
At that time, that servant received those horses, constantly tending them without fail or injury;
thus, for sixty billion white horses, he provided food costing one hundred taels of gold per day.
At that time, Changxin (Constant Faith) thought thus: "My body is but one, while the horses are many;
how difficult, how difficult it is to keep these animals unharmed! These horses are wicked and gallop out of control;
by what skillful means can they now be protected?"
Then, relying upon his teacher’s mastery of esoteric arts, he used the power of those arts to transform himself into ten million white horses.
Amidst these sixty billion white horses, he manifested transformed horses that neighed and whinnied, raising a great sound and proclaiming thus: "Every horse shall perform prostrations."
At that time, there was a medium-sized transformed horse that would always go forward to perform prostrations first;
all the other horses followed suit in their prostrations.
Once these acts were completed, the transformed horse would punish even minor faults by killing them, so that all the horses further submitted to its transformation.
Constantly believing that all his vows will be fully accomplished, he harbors no heart of anxiety or wonder.
Constantly believing, he further reflects:
"All these horses have been transformed by me; with the exception of the gold used for their equipment, they have performed wholesome deeds to transform their defiled retribution."
He addressed the horses, making this proclamation:
"My body and yours as well, in past lives, harbored regret in our hearts;
We fully committed all manner of evil karmic obstructions, And were thus born in this place as both slaves and horses."
At all times, one lacks sovereignty, oppressed by the suffering of illness and distracted by hunger and cold;
for a moment, one finds no peace or happiness.
If one does not perform wholesome deeds in this life, one will likewise receive such retribution in future lives; go on, go on—there will be no time of escape.
Just as it is fitting for you various animals to set aside your own provisions to offer to the field of merit,
so that through a moment’s hunger and thirst you may attain long-lasting joy—
do not let this leisurely time pass in vain; how much more so for you who possess the bodies of animals!
"When will you cultivate yourselves while your forms are defiled and your minds turbid?
It would be fitting for you to follow my transformation without opposition.
In that land there is a most excellent bird named *Ghoṣābhigargita-prabodhana* (Awakening through Elegant Sound).
The voice of this bird was inconceivable; upon hearing its sound, people were moved to great compassion and lamentation.
At that time, those six billion horses, having heard what Changxin had said, simultaneously let out a great cry of wailing that continued for ten days without ceasing.
The resonant neighing of these horses is equal, in every respect, to the awakening songs of birds;
there is no distinction between them.
Take one hundred measures of gold and divide them into two parts: let one part serve as the means for growth and sustenance.
One portion was set aside as the field of merit; for this field of merit, fifty taels of gold were used to fashion a single image of Vajra-Buddha, totaling sixty billion such images.
The supreme, foremost, great white horse, named Dīrghāyus-varṇa-vicitra-darśana,
along with Sadāśraddha and all the other horses, have all died; in their second birth, they are all humans,
belonging to the same retinue and never separated from one another, leaving the household life to study the Way and practice diligently.
Those six billion renunciants were all named Aśvaghoṣa with no other names,
for they received their names from the past.
Those sixty billion white horses of that time are now these sixty billion Aśvaghoṣas.
In my very first life, I was seen as a dappled horse; in this present life, I am merely this body of mine.
In my third birth, I was also a human being, following the World-Honored One as he practiced the bodhisattva path.
In my fourth birth, I again attained human form, following the World-Honored One as he cultivated the practice of patience.
Passing through five hundred successive births, in a subsequent life, due to the causes and conditions of anger, he obtained the body of a heavy serpent and underwent great suffering;
in the next birth, he took the body of a large fish, and in the following birth, he again obtained the body of a serpent.
With this serpent body, he went to the place where the World-Honored One was.
Casting his body down in repentance, he gave rise to shame and remorse; expressing his intent through verses, he resolved upon the Great Mind (*mahācitta*).
In his subsequent birth, he attained the human state (*manuṣyasabhāgatā*), and following the World-Honored One, he made a vow of affiliation.
Then the World-Honored One made this aspiration:
When I have attained the perfection of the path to enlightenment and proclaim ten billion sūtras, universally benefiting sentient beings through both extensive and concise teachings,
I shall then make this vow: to compose one hundred śāstras of elucidation, divided to benefit sentient beings through both extensive and concise teachings.
Just as the World-Honored One, through successive lifetimes, fulfilled the ocean of causal practices and dwelt upon the mountain-king throne of the Dharma-realm;
so too shall I gradually cultivate these causal deeds and realize entry into the eighth stage, the Immovable.
I then went to where the World-Honored One was, prostrated with my head at his feet, and stood to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One said to me:
"While you and I dwelt together in the same place, you made a vow that served as a causal condition for our connection."
"As it is fitting, you shall compose the treatises and instructions so that the True Dharma may flourish after my parinirvāṇa.
I then prostrated once more with palms joined and addressed the World-Honored One as follows:
'I do not yet know the method for composing treatises; I am utterly ignorant and have no realization whatsoever.'"
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, for the sake of this deluded child, will open my understanding by expounding the teachings of the treatise.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed me, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!"
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect well upon it; I shall explain it to you in detail.
Son of good family, the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas is immeasurable and boundless;
even if one were to speak for incalculable eons, it would never be exhausted, nor does it have any boundaries. Such is this immeasurable ocean of the Dharma-treasury.
Whether the treatise be explained extensively or in brief, it encompasses all things without exception;
this is called the teaching of the composed treatise.
I again harbor doubts and offer this request:

The ocean of Dharma gates is immeasurable and boundless; I have not yet filled the ocean of merit and wisdom, nor have I reached the ultimate within the stage of training. How could I possibly uphold them all without exception?
At that time, the World-Honored One said to me:

"There is a compendium of the fundamental dharmas of immeasurable schools; if one fully compiles these fundamental dharmas of the various schools, it is called 'the exposition of the treasury that compiles all dharmas.'"
I also made this further declaration:
"What is called the fundamental dharma of the school? Is its number known?"
At that time, the World-Honored One said to me:
"Regarding the great ocean of thirty-four dharmas, if there is a proponent who possesses these dharmas,
his discourse is called the 'Ocean-like Discourse of Perfect Name and Phrase.'"
If there are proponents who do not possess [this completeness], their discourse is called "partial" or "treatises of limited wisdom.
Now, relying upon thirty-four factors, I shall provide an exhaustive and systematic exposition without omission.
Although the categories of causes and conditions are immeasurable, they are summarized and briefly explained in this manner.

Thus has been explained the Great Section on the Determinative Analysis of Manifesting the Original Cause, Establishing Certainty, and Removing Doubts to Generate Faith. What are its characteristics?
The verse says:
"May this Ocean of Treatises, complete in its perfection, pervade all inconceivable lands as numerous as atoms."
The immeasurable sun of prajñā has arisen, Dispelling the boundless darkness of ignorance;
It transforms into the great ocean of the Triple Gem, A treasury of merit where nothing is contrary to the Dharma.
Without being entreated, its influence is universally pervasive; Without being exhorted, it is spontaneously accomplished.
